subject: Regional control map + SIG/CAIQ package request
messages:
From: MediMeta Security Team <security@medimeta.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SIG mapping and CAIQ package for regional hosting boundaries

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking the time on the call earlier. As a follow-up, our security group needs a compact packet showing how Redwood maps SIG controls to the CAIQ and SOC 2 scope for our planned EU-only pilot. Specifically we need:

- A CAIQ XLSX with our cells filled where possible (we received the empty CAIQ template attached).
- A short control map (one page) that shows which SIG sections demonstrate boundary controls for: VPC isolation, peering, KMS partitioning, and egress filtering.
- A network drawing that shows the private endpoint/privatelink topology and where traffic egresses to a customer-managed transit VPC.

Can you also confirm whether the dedicated EU deployment can be restricted to a single tenant pool (no shared GPUs) and whether HSM-backed KMS can be provisioned per-tenant? We have a hard requirement for key separation.

Appreciate a response this week if possible — we are on a tight procurement schedule.

Best,
Alice Turner
Security Program Manager
MediMeta

Attachment: medimeta_caiq_template.xlsx
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@medimeta.com>, MediMeta Security Team <security@medimeta.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SIG mapping and CAIQ package for regional hosting boundaries

Alice — thanks for the clear list. We can put together a concise packet. Quick answers up front: 

- Yes — we can run your pilot in an EU-only dedicated capacity (single-tenant GPU pool is available under our Dedicated offering).
- HSM-backed KMS can be provisioned as a customer-managed key (BYOK) per tenancy in Dedicated; we will include the key separation runbook and HSM-assurance note in the packet.
- The privatelink diagram will show the peering arrangement and the egress path to your transit VPC; we will annotate CIDR ranges and ACL expectations.

I will pull the CAIQ answers and a SIG-to-CAIQ control map. Irene and Sofia are copied — Irene will confirm the KMS/HSM language and Sofia will attach the VPC diagram and peering notes.

We expect to send the packet by EOD tomorrow. If you need the CAIQ in a particular cell format (e.g., blanked for legal), let us know.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Solutions Security
Redwood Inference
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Request: SIG mapping and CAIQ package for regional hosting boundaries

Folks — forwarding Alice's ask. Action items: 

- Irene: prepare a short (bullet) KMS/HSM assurance note that explicitly states whether HSM-backed keys can be unique per customer, what the key rotation cadence is, and how audit logs for key access are surfaced. Label it "KMS Partitioning — Medimeta".
- Sofia: produce a 1-page network diagram that shows: privatelink endpoint in eu-west-1, dedicated GPU pool CIDR, peer to customer transit VPC, and egress path (with NACL/Security Group callouts). Export as PNG and also include a separate text file with the peer setup steps (support for BGP or static routes).
- I will author the SIG->CAIQ control map (one pager) and fill the CAIQ where we can. Use the CAIQ template Alice attached as the source.

Schedule: let us aim for a consolidated packet by tomorrow 18:00 UTC. If capacity or legal redlines are required, flag them immediately.

Thanks — Grace
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
To: MediMeta Security Team <security@medimeta.com>, Alice Turner <alice.turner@medimeta.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SIG mapping and CAIQ package for regional hosting boundaries — packet attached

Alice / Medimeta team — attaching the requested package. Summary of what is included below.

Attachments: Redwood_CAIQ_responses_20260829.pdf; SIG_questionnaire_medimeta.xlsx; vpc_peering_diagram_medimeta.png

Executive summary:
- Dedicated EU capacity: confirmed. Single-tenant GPU pools can be reserved and scoped to your account under a Dedicated contract; see "Dedicated tenancy" section in the attached control map.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-provided keys via our BYOK flow; HSM-backed key material can be stored in a dedicated partition and access is restricted by role-based controls. Audit logs (key usage and wrap/unwrap) are available and included in the evidence bundle. The attached KMS note spells out rotation, split knowledge, and emergency key procedures.
- Network topology: privatelink endpoint terminates into your dedicated kuma-subnet; peering is via an encrypted private peering connection to your transit VPC. We documented CIDR ranges and recommend static route advertisement for predictable egress.
- SIG / CAIQ mapping: SIG sections most relevant to boundary controls are highlighted; cross-reference table maps each SIG control to the CAIQ question and our evidence artifact (SOC 2 section or design doc).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether the packet meets your procurement checklist or if you need additional SOC 2 evidence (test file or auditor contact).
2) If acceptable, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with our infra/security engineers to go over the network diagram and BGP/static route options.

Thanks — happy to iterate quickly.

—
Grace O'Connor
Director, Solutions Security
Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
